page: Microsoft Azure D48nlds_v6 is a specialized virtual machine configuration belonging to the Dnldv6 family, hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is provisioned with 48 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs based on an Intel processor platform and 96.0 GB of system memory. Operating at a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core, this configuration targets workloads that prioritize high processor core density without requiring the higher memory footprint standard in general-purpose cloud instances.

A key feature of the D48nlds_v6 instance is the integration of 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside premium remote storage capabilities. It features zero hardware GPU accelerators. With its combination of high vCPU capacity, reduced memory density, and large local NVMe storage, the instance avoids the cost overhead of excess memory while supplying substantial low-latency local drive performance.

Workloads best aligned with the D48nlds_v6 include high-throughput batch compute tasks, build and compilation pipelines, network-intensive appliances, and distributed data processing frameworks that utilize local disk caching and require compute parallelization rather than memory-resident dataset storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D48nlds_v6 is a compute-focused instance within the Dnldv6 series, operating under Microsoft Hyper-V on x86_64 Intel hardware. The virtual machine delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs paired with 96.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 2835 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage and support for premium storage tiers, with no auxiliary GPU acceleration. By limiting system RAM to 2.0 GB per core, this instance provides a cost-efficient profile for organizations requiring high parallel compute capacity and substantial low-latency local storage without paying for unused memory allocations. Common operational deployments include high-concurrency batch processing, software compilation, CI/CD runners, and computational workloads that leverage local NVMe storage for temporary data caching.
